F-CAP01-01.note: Resolved by cross-subsystem trace on 2026-07-22. POST /api/live/watch directly exposes site_override and room_override. The route is covered by the app-wide token/session and CSRF hooks when authentication is configured; auth-unconfigured deployments intentionally allow API access. The original SSRF boundary was therefore reachable. Since v3.66.590, watch() applies _host_on_cam_allowlist to the override path before creating a recording; private, link-local, and arbitrary non-cam hosts are rejected. Regression: tests/test_cap01_watch_override_host.py.

F-RUN01-02.note: Resolved by cross-subsystem trace on 2026-07-22. use_ytdlp_fallback is an opt-in per-site field and the fallback consumes the runner job URL. Normal HTTP enqueue paths reduce practical reachability of a leading-dash value, but source/plugin/config ingestion makes the subprocess boundary worth defending independently. Since v3.66.543, _build_ytdlp_cmd inserts a bare -- immediately before the URL, preventing every value from entering yt-dlp's option surface. Regression: tests/test_run01_ytdlp_argv_sep.py.

F-RUN01-03.note: Resolved by SETTINGS trace on 2026-07-22. disk_threshold_gb is covered by site_editor.NUMERIC_RANGES and the direct-PUT numeric backstop. bandwidth_target_mbps is a permitted per-site field but is not in that validator table, while hand-edited configuration can bypass route validation entirely. Since v3.66.548, the runner enforcement boundary uses _finite_config_float for both fields so NaN, infinity, and non-numeric values fall back safely. Regressions: tests/test_run01_numeric_nan_gate.py and tests/test_isfinite_numeric_backstop.py.
